title: RegradeEnvelope
description: Structured stdout of `cowork-harness regrade <run-dir>… --scenario <scenario.yaml> --output-format json` (SPEC §11). A covered surface of the 1.0 compatibility contract (SPEC §12): the frame, each `runs[]` entry's keys, the assertion-entry keys declared here, the enums and the error envelope's `error.code` / `refusals[]` / `runs[]`. Removing or renaming a key or an enum value, or changing a key's type or meaning, is MAJOR; adding a key or an enum value is MINOR — treat an unknown `docMatchesLive` as not `true`. This schema is deliberately permissive (no `additionalProperties: false`) so an additive change does not break a consumer validating with an older copy of the keys; an older copy does reject a new ENUM value. NOT covered: the regrade OUTPUT FILE (`turns/<N>/regrade/…json`) — its name, layout and contents are experimental; `regradeFile` is covered only as a key holding its path. An assertion entry's other keys (`assertion`, `message`, `judgeUsage`, `judgePromptHash`, `judgeTransport`, `judgeAttempts`, `judgedDoc`, `composedDoc`, `pairwise`, `semanticEvidence`) follow the RunResult assertion entry, which is not pinned field by field. Two shapes: a completed re-grade (`error: null`, exit 0 or 1) and the shared error envelope (exit 2).

oneOf.title: CompletedRegrade
oneOf.description: Every run dir was re-graded and its regrade file written. `ok` is true iff every re-graded assert passed (exit 0); false on exit 1.

judgeCostUsd.description: Sum of the priced judge calls over every run dir, retries included. Absent when none was priced — never 0 for unknown.

unpricedGrades.description: Grades with no price over every run dir; above 0, `judgeCostUsd` is a floor.

oneOf.title: ErrorEnvelope
oneOf.description: The shared error envelope (exit 2): a usage error; a refusal before any judge call — a drift, unchecked-content or scrub refusal carries `error.code` and lists every refused run dir in `refusals[]`, any other refusal carries no code; or a failure writing a regrade file after earlier run dirs were graded, whose reports are in `runs`.

refusals.description: Every run dir refused for its evidence or because a part of the judge's input cannot be proven scrubbed with a set covering the run's, one entry per run dir and code (a dir refused for several gets one per code).

scrubSet.description: A scrub refusal: why the run's scrub set is not proven covered — the run records no fingerprint (`legacy`, harness < 4.4), it recorded why it has none (`unrecorded`: its key was unusable; see `scrubSetDetail`), its fingerprint is unreadable (`mangled`), it was made under another installation key (`key`), or this process's set lacks a string the run scrubbed (`smaller`).

scrubSetDetail.description: `scrubSet: unrecorded`: the run's own reason (its key's path and defect).

rubricLines.description: `rubric_unverifiable`: per assert, the rubric line indexes not proven.

evidenceSections.description: `evidence_unverifiable`: the sections not proven, each by the index of the assert (in the scenario re-graded) whose document to be sent carries it.

runs.description: After a failure writing a regrade file: the run dirs graded and written before it.

code.description: On an evidence refusal: `doc_drift` when any run dir's kept evidence differs from what the live judge read, else `unchecked_content`, else the first scrub refusal in the order `task_unverifiable`, `rubric_unverifiable`, `evidence_unverifiable`, `reference_unverifiable` (a part of the judge's input — the pairwise task line, a rubric line, a section of the evidence, a reference — cannot be proven scrubbed with a set covering the run's; `--allow-scrub-change` accepts it). `no_semantic_asserts` (category usage): the scenario has no semantic_matches or semantic_pairwise assert, so there is nothing to re-grade.

LiveDocDrift.description: A drift in one LIVE assert's document, rebuilt from the live inputs. `liveAssertionIndex` is the assert's position in the live run's `assertions[]`; an empty `sections` means only the whole-document hash differs.

scrubAcceptedBy.description: Present when a part of the judge's input could not be proven scrubbed with a set covering the run's and was graded anyway: the flag that accepted it (`--allow-scrub-change`). Absent when every part was proven.

metrics.description: The scenario's declared metrics, re-read from the kept work dir as it is now, in the RunResult.metrics shape (one entry per declared id, in order; exactly one of value / unavailable). A file whose bytes no longer match the run's own recorded post-run hash (RunResult.workspaceFiles) is `pruned`. Absent when the scenario declares none.

regradeFile.description: Path of the file written. The key is covered; the file's name, layout and contents are experimental.

docMatchesLive.description: The run's value: false whenever `liveDocDrift` is non-empty; otherwise the worst over its asserts (false, live_refused, unknown, scope_changed, true; not_graded only when every assert is). The signal to consume.

liveDocDrift.description: The drift detected and accepted with --allow-doc-drift; [] when none was found.

RegradedAssertion.description: Only the keys below are covered. The entry also carries the RunResult assertion entry's other keys (assertion, message, judgeUsage, judgePromptHash, judgeTransport, judgeAttempts, judgedDoc, composedDoc, pairwise, semanticEvidence), which are not pinned field by field.

assertionIndex.description: The assert's position in the scenario's `assert:` list.

docMatchesLive.description: This assert's own document: false also when it carries a file an accepted drift is in.

judgeModel.description: The model id the judge answered as.

judgeModelRequested.description: The model this re-grade asked its judge for (--judge-model, else the assert's judge_model, else the default), on an entry a judge read. A kept entry carries the one it was graded with, if any.

DocMatch.description: Adding a value is MINOR; treat an unknown value as not `true`.
